newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Read our lips, say rebels: Mobutu has to go.
newsitem.headline: Read our lips, say rebels: Mobutu has to go.

text.p: Nothing short of the departure from power of Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko can stop a rebel march on the capital Kinshasa, a senior spokesman for the rebel alliance said on Friday.

In case anyone had the impression from United Nations or South African mediators that some graceful transition period or power-sharing deal was an option, rebel foreign minister Bizima Karaha called a news conference to correct that mistaken view.

"We're going to kick them out. We've got the will and the means. We're not negotiating for power sharing, not ever," he told reporters in rebel-held Lubumubashi, the biggest Zairean city in the hands of Laurent Kabila's anti-Mobutu alliance.

Kabila is ready to speak to Mobutu, he said. "That's not a problem. It's what they're going to talk about. They're not friends, and they have no other business. There's only one question: Mobutu must go."
Kabila said earlier in a telephone interview from Lubumbashi, current headquarters of his rebel alliance, that he would talk only about a transfer of power.
"There will be no protracted negotiations with Mobutu, never, never," he said. "Maybe we have been misunderstood. The issue is about transfer of power, otherwise we march on Kinshasa."

There was speculation Mobutu and Kabila might meet in South Africa next week, but Karaha declined to talk about dates, focusing instead on what he saw as a misconception about the rebels "negotiating" position.
"We are negotiating the mode of departure of Mobutu...the modalities for the end of a dictatorial regime," he said.
If the man who has ruled Zaire for the past 32 years goes peacefully, he could avert a battle for Kinshasa. If not, the rebel army would push him out, Karaha said.

At talks in South Africa, the rebel side was ready to talk about Mobutu's security, his future, whether he has to go into exile and his vast personal fortune. "We want to re-import his money," Karaha said.
But he poured cold water on any talk of a ceasefire and utterly rejected any sort of modus vivendi with the Mobutu regime, or even the government's political opponents in Kinshasa.

"We don't want any cessation of hostilities. We want the end of the war and that can only come if the man who brought the war is kicked out," he said. "When Mobutu leaves, that will be the end of the war."
Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire accused the Mobutu government of stalling and warned that would not work for long.
"This (talking) is not going to go beyond June, as we've said before," justice minister Mwenge Kogolo said.

Asked if the Alliance was willing to find a place in power for the political opposition to Mobutu that exists in Kinshasa, Karaha said: "There's no peaceful opposition in this country. if it's peaceful it's not opposition."
There was "nothing in between" Mobutu's reactionary regime and the rebel Alliance, he said. "You're either with Mobutu or with the people."
